root_cause.text: The teardown order in ext4_put_super was changed to unregister sysfs before flushing the super update workqueue (s_sb_upd_work), allowing the work to run after the kobject's kernfs_node has been freed via kobject_del(), causing a use-after-free in sysfs_notify().
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly state: "moved ext4_unregister_sysfs() before flushing s_sb_upd_work ... introduced a use-after-free because update_super_work calls ext4_notify_error_sysfs() -> sysfs_notify() which accesses the kobject's kernfs_node after it has been freed by kobject_del()." The fix adds a mutex and checks s_kobj.state_in_sysfs to avoid the call when sysfs is already torn down.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call to sysfs_notify on the superblock kobject after it has been freed due to incorrect teardown order in ext4_put_super leads to use-after-free.
Sysfs group removal before flushing the workqueue allows work items to run after the kobject's kernfs_node is freed.
Deleting the kobject frees its kernfs_node, causing subsequent sysfs_notify in workqueue to access freed memory.
Flushing the workqueue after kobject_del means work items still in flight will use the already freed kobject, triggering use-after-free.
Destroying the workqueue after flush does not prevent use-after-free if work was still scheduled before flush.
